result.title: Contrastive fine-tuning against stain and scanner bias improves robustness and downstream performance across pathology foundation models
result.summary: Histopathology foundation models achieve strong performance across diverse downstream tasks, yet their representations have been shown to encode scanner- and site-specific biases, creating generalization gaps and potentially limiting real-world utility. We introduce SPECTRA (Scanner and Pathology Embedding Contrastive Tuning for Robust Alignment), a model-agnostic contrastive learning post-training framework which explicitly encourages scanner- and stain-robust representations, to optimize performance and generalization on downstream applications. Using parameter-efficient LoRA adapters trained on matched multi-scanner and multi-stain whole-slide images sourced from the PLISM dataset, our method aligns spatially corresponding regions across acquisition conditions (scanner, stain), using other locations within each candidate condition as negatives. SPECTRA improved PathoROB robustness index, gene-expression prediction on HEST, slide-level classification AUC on CPTAC, and held-out PLISM retrieval for every model. Overall tile-level classification on THUNDER also improved, with exceptions for segmentation and calibration tasks. We open-source our training and evaluation codebases and release adapters and model weights for selected backbones.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SPECTRA：一种模型无关的对比学习后训练框架，用 LoRA 适配器在多扫描仪、多染色的配对全切片图像上对齐空间对应区域的表示，以提升病理基础模型的染色／扫描仪鲁棒性与下游性能。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「对采集条件不变、同时保留下游任务信息」的对比式表示约束，可能与 LVR 中视觉细节保留与无关变异不变性之间的权衡问题相关，可供核查强制不变性是否会挤掉任务必要的视觉信息。
